evidence.quote: we recorded a $15.93 billion charge in the third quarter of 2025, of which $14.03 billion was a valuation allowance against our U.S. federal deferred tax assets as of the enactment date of OBBBA... Our provision for income taxes in 2025 increased $17.17 billion or 207% compared to 2024, primarily due to an increase in the effective tax rate.

input.label: SUPPORTED
input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Meta's net income for fiscal year 2025 decreased compared with fiscal year 2024. Evidence E2 and E10 from Meta's 10-K filing for the year ended December 31, 2025 clearly show that net income was $60,458 million in FY2025 compared to $62,360 million in FY2024, representing a decrease of $1,902 million (approximately 3.05%). The numeric check confirms this decrease with a yoy_change of -0.0305. The evidence review confirms that E2, E7, E8, E9, and E10 all ENTAIL the claim with EXACT_MATCH or COMPATIBLE_AFTER_VERIFIED_DERIVATION period compatibility.

Challenge H1 (restatements): No evidence of restatements or corrections to the net income figures was found in the retrieved passages.

Challenge H2 (one-time charges): While E14 and E15 mention potential charges related to impairments and other items as forward-looking risk factors, no specific evidence was found documenting one-time charges that would materially affect the interpretation of the net income decrease claim itself.

Challenge H3 (tax changes): Evidence E18 confirms that there was indeed a significant tax-related impact in 2025. Meta recorded a $15.93 billion charge in Q3 2025 related to OBBBA tax legislation, and the provision for income taxes increased $17.17 billion (207%) compared to 2024. However, this challenge does not refute the claim - it merely explains a driver of the decrease. The claim simply states that net income decreased, without specifying any cause, so the presence of tax-related drivers does not contradict the factual assertion that net income decreased.

The verdict remains SUPPORTED because the evidence definitively establishes that net income decreased from FY2024 to FY2025, which is exactly what the claim asserts.
